stem: Who came up with the idea of dynamic programming in the 1950s?
explanation: The course credits Richard Bellman with dynamic programming in the 1950s.

stem: Which two properties show that a problem can be solved with dynamic programming?
explanation: The two signs of DP suitability are overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.

stem: Binary search is a dynamic programming problem because it has overlapping subproblems.
explanation: Binary search has no overlapping subproblems; each sub-problem searches a unique part of the array, so it is divide and conquer.

stem: Which technique speeds up programs by storing the results of function calls so the same input is not processed again?
explanation: Memoization caches the results of earlier calls and returns them for repeated inputs.

stem: What is the time complexity of the Floyd–Warshall algorithm on n nodes?
explanation: Floyd–Warshall has three nested loops, giving O(n³).

stem: Which one is not a dynamic programming algorithm or problem in the course?
explanation: Merge sort combines sub-problems that do not overlap, so it is not a DP problem.

stem: In the memoized (top-down) version, the look-up table is filled on demand, so not every entry is necessarily filled.
explanation: Tabulation fills every entry from the first; memoization fills the table only for sub-problems actually needed.

stem: Which statements about the bottom-up (tabulation) approach are correct?

options.text: It is usually faster than memoization
It fills the table only on demand

explanation: Bottom-up removes recursion and its overhead and is faster; filling on demand describes memoization.
source: CSC 551 Study Session 3, 3.6; CSC 551 Study Session 6, 6.7
